svg.aria-label: Design decisions: NAT stays at the edge. The STC modem and the ISR 4331 handle NAT. OPNsense adds none of its own, so it filters and inspects traffic with the real internal addresses. Routing happens at the core. The core 3850 is the gateway for every VLAN and relays DHCP, leaving the firewall to guard traffic in and out of the network. One 20G uplink. Two 10G links in an LACP port-channel join the core and access switches. That doubles the bandwidth, and the uplink stays up if one cable fails. Split hypervisor networking. Proxmox is managed on VLAN 10, while its VMs use a separate trunk for VLANs 20 and 40, so host management never shares a link with VM traffic. Two APs, two networks. An access point on each floor broadcasts the Internal and Guest SSIDs, each mapped to its own VLAN. 802.11r lets devices roam between floors without dropping. Two DHCP servers, one relay. The core relays every DHCP request. Internal clients get addresses from the domain controller, while guests and cameras get theirs from OPNsense, so neither ever talks to a server. Guests and cameras kept apart. Access lists on the core keep both VLANs away from the trusted networks. Guests only reach the internet, and the admin workstation can still reach in to manage the cameras. Automation. Ansible manages device configuration, so every change is repeatable, reviewable and tracked.
svg.title: Design decisions
